scope: current Hebrew source and encoding closure

notes: Every word of the body text was compared with zikhronot_open (s212 part), the verses Genesis 8:1 through Jeremiah 31:19 with their rubrics, and zikhronot_close up to וּזְכָר־לָנוּ יְיָ. Verse extent and the rubric wording וְנֶאֱמַר / וּבְדִבְרֵי קָדְשְׁךָ כָּתוּב לֵאמֹר / וְעַל־יְדֵי עֲבָדֶיךָ הַנְּבִיאִים כָּתוּב לֵאמֹר match. On this page the rubrics have no comma after them, and the current text has none.
The running header (96 תפלת מוסף ליום ראשון של ראש השנה 96) is not encoded. That is acceptable for a running head. Its faint pointing is out of scope.

The three Torah verses carry printed accents (band1 and band2). In Genesis 8:1: a ring/pashta-shaped mark above the final mem of the first אֱלֹהִים, above the end of הַחַיָּה and above the end of רוּחַ; a '<'-shaped mark under the first וַיִּזְכֹּר; a row of sublinear strokes under וַיַּעֲבֵר. In Exodus 2:24: a ring above the second אֱלֹהִים, a '<' under וַיִּזְכֹּר and strokes under נַאֲקָתָם. In Leviticus 26:42: a small ring above the final ף of the first וְאַף, plus sublinear marks. The current text has none of these marks.
The Psalms and Prophets quotations on this page show vowels only. No supralinear accents are visible where the masoretic text would put them, for example over הָלֹךְ or אוֹתָךְ.

The text was checked against zikhronot_close (s214 part), covenant_verse, zikhronot_blessing, shofarot_open and the start of shofarot_verses. The small-type parentheticals (שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב) and (כָּל) are present in the encoding.

Exodus 19:16 has printed accents: rings above both וַיְהִי and above הַשְּׁלִישִׁי and כָּבֵד; a caret-shaped mark at מְאֹד; a row of sublinear marks under וַיֶּחֱרַד and under בַּמַּחֲנֶה. Exodus 19:19 has a ring above וַיְהִי, a caret at מְאֹד, and sublinear marks under יְדַבֵּר and יַעֲנֶנּוּ. Exodus 20:15 has a ring between הָעָם and רֹאִים, a ring above וְאֵת, and a dot cluster above הַלַּפִּידִם. None of these are encoded.

In this prayer text the print puts a comma after אֵשׁ and after כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ. It also puts a comma after each וְנֶאֱמַר that introduces a verse on the lower half of the page. The current text drops them.
The Exodus 20:15 continuation is printed with accents: a ring above הָעָם, a three-dot segolta-like cluster above וַיָּנֻעוּ, and marks under עָשֵׁן, וַיַּרְא and וַיַּעַמְדוּ.

Numbers 10:10 is printed with accents: a short overline above the final ם of וּבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם, a three-dot cluster above the final ם of חָדְשֵׁכֶם, and sublinear marks under וּתְקַעְתֶּם, עַל, וְעַל, זִבְחֵי and לָכֶם. The overline and the dot cluster sit exactly where the zarqa and segolta of the masoretic verse fall, which confirms these are cantillation and not damage. They are not encoded.

Isaiah 27:13 and Zechariah 9:14 have no printed cantillation. The supralinear positions where the masoretic text has zaqef or other upper accents (אַשּׁוּר and בְּאֶרֶץ in Isaiah 27:13; יֵרָאֶה and יִתְקָע in Zechariah 9:14; תֵבֵל in Isaiah 18:3) are clean in band2 and band3. The only sublinear marks are vowels or meteg-like strokes. So nothing should be added there.

The commas printed after the rubrics on this page are dropped in the current text: after לֵאמֹר twice, after וְנֶאֱמַר five times, and in יָהּ, הַלְלוּיָהּ. Zechariah 9:15a ends in a colon in the print, not a period.

In shofarot_close, the print shows כְּמִצְוָה followed by the small parenthetical נ״א כִּמְצֻוָּה. The human adjudication (answer 8) already resolved this and the encoding matches it, so it is not raised again.

questions.question: These verses are printed with cantillation but are encoded with vowels only. Should the encoding transcribe the printed accents? If so, someone needs to map each glyph to Unicode from a higher-resolution scan. In this typeface the ring may stand for pashta or telisha, and the '<' may be mahpakh. I cannot settle every sublinear accent at this resolution, and I have deliberately not supplied them from memory. This needs to be decided before approval.

guideline_findings: Versification: Exodus 20 'וְכָל־הָעָם רֹאִים' is encoded as exodus/20/18. JLPTEI-3 'Versification' says canonical verse URNs follow Leningrad numbering, where this verse is 20:15. See the correction above. The local stem quotes/exodus_20_18 should change with it.

Alternatives vs conditions: (שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב) in musaf_zikhronot_blessing, and (כָּל) in musaf_shofarot_open according to the input alternatives, are encoded as tei:choice/j:option. The guideline ('Note the distinction from a condition') says text that some communities add and others omit is a condition (j:conditional), not an alternate. כְּמִצְוָה / נ״א כִּמְצֻוָּה is a true alternate wording, so j:option is right there.

Printed cantillation is present but not encoded in the Torah verses on s212, s214 and s216, so the Hebrew is not yet a faithful transcription. No cantillation should be added to Psalms, Isaiah 18/27, Zechariah 9, Jeremiah, Ezekiel or Leviticus 26:45, because none is printed there.

Zechariah 9:15 verse-part 'adonai_tzevaot_yagen': per 'Sub-verse scope', the part has to be declared in opensiddur/common/subverse.py. Because the quotation stops mid-verse, a part is also needed where the rest of the verse (וְאָכְלוּ …) begins. I did not verify this; the XML only has a bare verse-part terminator.
Double spaces after the rubrics (e.g. 'וְנֶאֱמַר  ' in musaf_shofarot_verses.xml) are cosmetic. They should be normalized when the commas are added.
